# Tobit Chapter 5 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_005_page_001.jpg

---

**1** "I'll do everything you've told me, Father," Tobias said.

**2** "But how am I supposed to collect the money? He doesn't know me and I don't know him. What kind of proof do I bring so he'll trust me enough to hand it over? And I've never even been to Media — I wouldn't know which road to take."

**3** Tobit said, "We each wrote out a promissory note, then tore it in half and kept one piece. I put my half with the money for safekeeping. And that was twenty years ago now. So find someone dependable who can make the trip with you — we'll pay him when you get back — and go get the money from Gabael."

**4** Tobias went out to look for a travel companion, and there was Raphael — an angel, though Tobias had no idea.

**5** "Could you come with me to Rages in Media?" Tobias asked him. "Do you know the area?"

**6** "I can make the trip," the angel told him. "I know those roads well. I've stayed with our kinsman Gabael."

**7** "Wait here," Tobias said. "I'll just go tell my father."

**8** He ran inside: "Father — I found someone! One of our own people, a son of Israel."

"Bring him in," Tobit said. "I want to find out his tribe and make sure he's trustworthy before he travels with my son."

**9** Tobias stepped outside: "My father wants to meet you."

The man came in. Tobit spoke first, greeting him warmly. Raphael said, "May you have every happiness."

"Happiness?" Tobit said. "I'm a blind man — I can't see the light of heaven. I live in darkness like someone already dead. I'm a living corpse. I hear voices but I see nothing."

"Take heart," Raphael said to him. "God has healing in store for you, very soon. Take heart."

"My son wants to travel to Media," Tobit said. "Could you be his guide? I'll pay you well."

"I can go with him," he said. "I know the roads, and I've stayed with our kinsman Gabael in Rages. It's about two days from Ecbatana to Rages — it's up in the hill country."

**10** "Tell me something, brother," Tobit said. "What tribe are you from? What family?"

**11** "What tribe are you looking for?" he said.

"I want to know who you are," Tobit said, "what family you belong to, and your name."

**12** "I'm Azariah," he said. "Son of the great Ananias — one of your own kinsmen."

**13** "You're welcome here, brother!" Tobit said. "Don't be offended that I asked — it turns out you're from a fine family, my own people. I knew Ananias and Nathan, the sons of old Shemaiah. We used to go up to Jerusalem together for worship, offering the firstborn animals and the tithes. They were faithful men — they never got swept up in the idolatry our brothers fell into. You come from good stock, brother.

**14** Now — what should I pay you? A drachma a day, plus expenses, the same as I'd provide for my own son?

**15** And if you bring him back safely, I'll give you something extra on top."

They shook on it.

**16** Tobit said to Tobias: "Get ready to go, son, and travel with your brother. May God in heaven bless your journey and send his angel along with you."

The two of them headed out, and Tobias's dog came trotting along behind them.

**17** His mother Anna burst into tears. "Why are you sending my boy away?" she cried to Tobit. "He's the one we lean on — he's our hands and feet!

**18** Don't put money above our child. Whatever it costs, let that money be the price for keeping him safe.

**19** The life God has given us — that is enough."

**20** "Don't worry, dear," Tobit said. "He'll go safely and come back safely. You'll see him again with your own eyes.

**21** A good angel will be with him the whole way — his journey will be blessed, and he'll come home safe and sound."

She stopped crying.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **v. 4 — Dramatic irony**: "There was Raphael — an angel, though Tobias had no idea." The Greek announces this to the reader outright. PNEUMA makes the contrast stark: the reader knows everything; Tobias knows nothing. This dramatic irony is the engine of the entire story.
- **v. 9 — "I'm a living corpse"**: Tobit's self-description (*nekros zōn*) is rendered as "I'm a living corpse" — the sharpest English equivalent of a paradox that the Greek text leaves unexplained. His blindness is total, social, and spiritual isolation.
- **v. 9 — Raphael's "Take heart"**: Rendered twice, as in the Greek. This is not incidental repetition — it is reassurance from a being who actually knows the outcome.
- **v. 16 — The dog**: Retained because it signals the longer Sinaiticus recension and because the animal is a humanizing detail that marks the journey's beginning. It appears again in ch. 11 when the family is reunited.
- **vv. 17–19 — Anna's speech**: PNEUMA names her "Anna" (Greek *Hanna*) rather than "Hannah" for stylistic consistency with Deuterocanonical naming conventions. Her three-verse lament is kept intact — the emotional weight of a mother's grief must not be condensed.
- **v. 12 — Azariah**: The irony of a disguised angel giving a name meaning "the LORD has helped" is left implicit. PNEUMA trusts the reader to make the connection rather than annotating it. — PNEUMA
